summary: Iteration 7 — Tested new react-pdf viewer + bookmark feature. Backend: added 6 bookmark tests to test_digilib_api.py; all 28 pytest tests pass (100%). Frontend: react-pdf renders correctly, zoom/page controls work as specified, bookmark save + toast + class change works, anonymous flow correctly shows 'Masuk untuk menyimpan bookmark' toast and does NOT hit API. Regression flows OK. ONE BUG FOUND: bookmark persistence across reopen is broken when saved page == 1 (button reverts to 'Bookmark' instead of 'Ditandai · hal. 1').

ui_bugs.issue: On reopen, saved bookmark is only re-hydrated into `bookmarkPage` state when `data.page > 1`. When the user bookmarked page 1 (the only page in the demo PDF), reopening the viewer shows the button as 'Bookmark' with no `pdf-bookmarked` class, even though the backend correctly returns `{page: 1, updated_at: <iso>}`. Expected per spec: button should start as 'Ditandai · hal. 1' with class 'pdf-bookmarked'. Fix: move `setBookmarkPage(data.page)` outside the `data.page > 1` guard so it always reflects saved state; only the page-jump / jumpValue update should be guarded by `> 1`.

critical_code_review_comments: PdfViewer auto-save effect (App.js ~L549) fires an immediate PUT once numPages loads even if user hasn't navigated — this bookmarks page 1 automatically the first time an authenticated user opens any PDF. Consider guarding with a `hasUserNavigated` flag or only saving when pageNumber changes from initial value. Currently causes an unintended bookmark row on first visit.

server.py bookmark endpoint uses ObjectId(book_id) — good; returns 404 for malformed ids. Consider also validating that the book actually exists (currently upserts even for a valid-looking but non-existent ObjectId).
BookmarkIn only validates `page: int >= 1`. No upper bound — a malicious client could store an arbitrary huge int. Consider `Field(ge=1, le=100000)` or validating against actual numPages when known.
server.py still 870 lines — split into routers/modules recommended.
isBookmarked comparison uses `bookmarkPage === pageNumber`; combined with the persistence bug above, once fixed the semantics work but consider explicit typing (both are numbers).

rca_of_the_issue: PdfViewer effect at App.js ~L531 guards ALL bookmark-state hydration behind `if (data?.page && data.page > 1)`. That was likely meant to guard only the auto-jump (setPageNumber) so the viewer doesn't jump to page 1 unnecessarily. But it also skips `setBookmarkPage(data.page)`, so the `isBookmarked = bookmarkPage === pageNumber` comparison is `null === 1 = false` on reopen when the saved page is 1. Backend GET /api/bookmarks/{id} verified returning {page:1, updated_at:'…'} in pytest. Repro: login as andi, open Analisis Data dengan Python -> Baca online -> click Bookmark (toast OK, button becomes 'Ditandai · hal. 1') -> close pdf-viewer-close -> click Baca online again -> button now reads 'Bookmark' (no pdf-bookmarked class). Fix scope: 3 lines in App.js.
